claims.statement: Every nontrivial zero rho of zeta satisfies Re(rho)=1/2.
The existing c=2 trace/Frobenius/positive-index certificate is simultaneously extremal on online doubles and tight off-line pairs and cannot be improved using only those quantities.

For an absolutely summable spectral zero filter with critical-line center, any zeta zero with Re(rho) > 1/2 and nonzero multiplicity-weighted filter coefficient forces the filtered zero family to fail the subexponential bound (exposed right-side Laplace pole). Left-side zeros are excluded downstream via the zeta reflection rho -> 1 - conj(rho), never by imposing reflection symmetry on generic filters.

The filtered zero family of the natural Weil filter at center 1/2 equals, at every aperture a, the literature explicit-formula RHS of the right-translated test k(. - 2a), under exact C^2 compact-support hypotheses; absolute filter summability follows from EF_lit's summability clause.

For every hypothetical zeta zero strictly to the right of the critical line there exists an admissible pole-killed C^2 compactly supported Weil test (target-adaptive modulated bump through the pole-killer q'' - q/4) whose translated literature-RHS residual fails the subexponential bound.
